requirements.heading: Terminology
requirements.text: Strings referred to in this document, including ASCII strings, MUST be expressed in UTF-8.

requirements.heading: Framework for the Internationalization Extension
requirements.text: In order to permit future (although unanticipated) extensions, the EHLO response MUST NOT contain any parameters for this keyword.

requirements.heading: Framework for the Internationalization Extension
requirements.text: The SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client MUST ignore any parameters if they appear for this keyword; that is, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client MUST behave as if the parameters do not appear.

requirements.heading: Framework for the Internationalization Extension
requirements.text: If an SMTP server includes SMTPUTF8 in its EHLO response, it MUST be fully compliant with this version of this specification.

requirements.heading: Framework for the Internationalization Extension
requirements.text: One OPTIONAL parameter, SMTPUTF8, is added to the MAIL command.

requirements.heading: Framework for the Internationalization Extension
requirements.text: One OPTIONAL parameter, SMTPUTF8, is added to the VERIFY (VRFY) and EXPAND (EXPN) commands.

requirements.heading: Framework for the Internationalization Extension
requirements.text: Servers offering this extension MUST provide support for, and announce, the 8BITMIME extension [RFC6152].

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: An SMTP server that announces the SMTPUTF8 extension MUST be prepared to accept a UTF-8 string [RFC3629] in any position in which RFC 5321 specifies that a <mailbox> can appear.

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: Any domain name to be looked up in the DNS MUST conform to and be processed as specified for Internationalizing Domain Names in Applications (IDNA) [RFC5890].

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: When doing lookups, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client or server MUST either use a Unicode-aware DNS library, or transform the internationalized domain name to A-label form (i.e., a fully- qualified domain name that contains one or more A-labels but no U-labels) as specified in RFC 5890 [RFC5890].

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: An SMTP client that receives the SMTPUTF8 extension keyword in response to the EHLO command MAY transmit mailbox names within SMTP commands as internationalized strings in UTF-8 form.

requirements.text: It MAY send a UTF-8 header [RFC6532] (which may also include mailbox names in

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: It MAY transmit the domain parts of mailbox names within SMTP commands or the message header as A-labels or U-labels [RFC5890].

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: If the SMTPUTF8 SMTP extension is not offered by the SMTP server, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client MUST NOT transmit an internationalized email address and MUST NOT transmit a mail message containing internationalized mail headers as described in RFC 6532 [RFC6532] at any level within its MIME structure [RFC2045].

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: o If it is a Message Submission Agent (MSA) [RFC6409] [RFC5598], it MAY choose its own way to deal with this scenario using the wide discretion for changing addresses or otherwise fixing up and transforming messages allowed by RFC 6409.

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: o If it is not an MSA or is an MSA and does not choose to transform the message to one that does not require the SMTPUTF8 extension, it SHOULD reject the message.

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: If the latter choice is made, the notification process MUST conform to the requirements of RFC 5321, RFC 3464 [RFC3464], and RFC 6533 [RFC6533].

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: o As specified in Section 2.2.3 of RFC 5321, an SMTP client with additional information and/or knowledge of special circumstances MAY choose to requeue the message and try later and/or try an alternate MX host as specified in that section.

requirements.heading: The SMTPUTF8 Extension
requirements.text: If an SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server advertises the Delivery Status Notification (DSN) [RFC3461] extension, it MUST implement RFC 6533 [RFC6533].

requirements.heading: Extended Mailbox Address Syntax
requirements.text: That string MUST NOT contain any of the ASCII graphics or control characters.

requirements.heading: MAIL Command Parameter Usage
requirements.text: If the envelope or message being sent requires the capabilities of the SMTPUTF8 extension, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client MUST supply the SMTPUTF8 parameter with the MAIL command.

requirements.heading: MAIL Command Parameter Usage
requirements.text: If this parameter is provided, it MUST not accept a value.

requirements.heading: MAIL Command Parameter Usage
requirements.text: If the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client is aware that neither the envelope nor the message being sent requires any of the SMTPUTF8 extension capabilities, it SHOULD NOT supply the SMTPUTF8 parameter with the MAIL command.

requirements.heading: Non-ASCII Addresses and Reply-Codes
requirements.text: An SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client MUST NOT send an internationalized message to an SMTP server that does not support SMTPUTF8.

requirements.heading: Additional ESMTP Changes and Clarifications
requirements.text: When RFC 5321 specifies a domain name, the internationalized domain name SHOULD be in U-label form if the SMTPUTF8 extension is supported; otherwise, it SHOULD be in A-label form.

requirements.heading: The Initial SMTP Exchange
requirements.text: Since the SMTP client cannot know whether the SMTP server supports SMTPUTF8 until after it receives the response to the EHLO, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP client MUST send only ASCII (LDH label or A-label [RFC5890]) domains in the EHLO command.

requirements.heading: The Initial SMTP Exchange
requirements.text: If the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server provides domain names in the EHLO response, they MUST be in the form of LDH labels or A-labels.

requirements.heading: Mail eXchangers
requirements.text: If multiple DNS MX records are used to specify multiple servers for a domain (as described in Section 5 of RFC 5321 [RFC5321]), it is strongly advised that all or none of them SHOULD support the SMTPUTF8

requirements.heading: Trace Information
requirements.text: When an SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server adds a trace field to a message that was or will be transmitted with the SMTPUTF8 parameter included in the MAIL commands, that server SHOULD use the U-label form for internationalized domain names in the new trace field.

requirements.heading: MAIL Command
requirements.text: If an SMTP client follows this specification and sends any MAIL commands containing the SMTPUTF8 parameter, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server is permitted to use UTF-8 characters in the email address associated with 251 and 551 reply-codes, and the SMTP client MUST be able to accept and process them.

requirements.heading: MAIL Command
requirements.text: If a given MAIL command does not include the SMTPUTF8 parameter, the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server MUST NOT return a 251 or 551 response containing a non-ASCII mailbox.

requirements.heading: MAIL Command
requirements.text: Instead, it MUST transform such responses into 250 or 550 responses that do not contain non-ASCII addresses.

requirements.heading: VRFY and EXPN Commands and the SMTPUTF8 Parameter
requirements.text: commands SHOULD only be used after the SMTP client sees the EHLO response with the SMTPUTF8 keyword.

requirements.heading: VRFY and EXPN Commands and the SMTPUTF8 Parameter
requirements.text: An SMTP client that conforms to this specification MUST accept and correctly process replies to the VRFY and EXPN commands that contain UTF-8 strings.

requirements.heading: VRFY and EXPN Commands and the SMTPUTF8 Parameter
requirements.text: However, an SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server MUST NOT use UTF-8 strings in replies if the SMTP client does not specifically allow such replies by transmitting this parameter with the VRFY and EXPN commands.

requirements.heading: VRFY and EXPN Commands and the SMTPUTF8 Parameter
requirements.text: If the reply to a VRFY or EXPN command requires a UTF-8 string, but the SMTP client did not use the SMTPUTF8 parameter, then the SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP server MUST use either the reply-code 252 or 550.

requirements.heading: VRFY and EXPN Commands and the SMTPUTF8 Parameter
requirements.text: If a normal success response (i.e., 250) is returned, the response MAY include the full name of the user and MUST include the mailbox of the user.

requirements.heading: VRFY and EXPN Commands and the SMTPUTF8 Parameter
requirements.text: SMTPUTF8-aware SMTP servers MUST NOT include non-ASCII characters in replies except in the limited cases specifically permitted in this section.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: Mechanisms to automatically and quickly provide the origin or ownership of an internationalized email address SHALL be implemented for use by log readers that cannot easily read non-ASCII information.
